title: Japan's Shoe Etiquette Can Delay Paramedics
paragraphs: In Japan, it is customary to take off your shoes before entering someone's home. Paramedics follow this custom as well, but a fire department in Japan has warned that a polite habit related to shoes could actually slow them down.

In August 2026, the fire department in the city of Kanazawa posted a video on its official Instagram account. The video showed a simulated emergency in which paramedics entered a home and left their shoes at the entrance. While they were inside helping a patient, a resident neatly rearranged the paramedics' shoes. The video, which has been viewed more than half a million times, asks residents to leave the shoes exactly where the paramedics put them.

According to the fire department, paramedics do not take off their shoes randomly. Instead, they position them according to each crew member's role and the route they will take when they carry the patient out. For example, the leader of the ambulance crew carries the end of the stretcher where the patient's head is, while other members support it from the sides. If the shoes are lined up neatly or turned around, the paramedics may need extra time to find the right shoes while they are carrying the stretcher.
The fire department also warned that unnecessary movement can shake the patient and might even cause equipment, such as an oxygen mask, to come loose.

Firefighter Daisuke Yamashita said that, in their experience, rearranging the shoes can cause a delay of around 30 seconds. However, Yamashita also said that the paramedics appreciate the kindness behind the act.
Instead of tidying shoes, Yamashita suggested that residents prepare the patient's My Number card or another form of identification in advance.

The story was later reported by international media, including the British newspaper The Guardian. It also caused discussion online, as people in many other countries pointed out that emergency workers usually keep their shoes or boots on when entering a home.
